strongest_angle: Examine how the Super El Niño weather phenomenon drove a massive surge in water levels at the Iguazú Falls on the Brazil-Argentina border in October 2026, causing temporary closures and flooding across South America.

key_facts.fact: National park officials in Argentina temporarily closed Iguazú Falls after heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate in October 2026.
The Iguazú Falls form a complex of cascades spanning more than a mile across both the Brazil and Argentina border.
Heavy rains linked to El Niño caused flooding across swaths of Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay in October 2026.

numbers.label: River flow rate multiplier compared to normal
